ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is the transformer secondary winding, marked beside it as 10V; the two ends of the secondary are connected to a diamond-shaped bridge rectifier circuit composed of four diodes, and the right side is connected to a load. This circuit is a single-phase full-bridge rectifier circuit, not a center-tapped rectifier circuit. Reasoning: The 10V in the figure is treated as the AC RMS value. In a single-phase bridge rectifier, the maximum reverse voltage borne by each diode is equal to the peak value of the transformer secondary voltage, namely VRRM = Vm. The peak value Vm = 10 × √2 ≈ 14.14V. Therefore, the maximum reverse voltage that diode D needs to withstand is 14.14V.

raw_record.question_text: In the single-phase bridge rectifier circuit shown in the figure, what is the maximum reverse voltage that diode D can withstand?

method.method_draft: First identify the visual circuit as a full bridge rectifier, not a center-tapped rectifier. Take the secondary voltage shown in the image as 10 V RMS. Use the bridge-rectifier PIV relation for each diode: VRRM = Vm. Convert RMS to peak: Vm = 10 × √2 = 14.14 V. Therefore diode D must withstand a maximum reverse voltage of 14.14 V.
